successCriteria.description: A new knex migration under migrations/ adds a nullable `password_hash` column to `employees` using `t.text('password_hash')` (not `t.json`), with an `up` that alters the table to add the column and a `down` that drops it.

`Employee` in employee.model.ts exposes `passwordHash: string | null` alongside the existing canonical fields, and `CreateEmployeeInput` remains `Omit<Employee, 'id'>` (so create supplies passwordHash as null).

`IEmployeeRepository.findByManagerId(managerId, client?)` returns every employee whose `manager_id` equals the argument, mapped through the existing `mapRow`, as an array (possibly empty) without throwing on empty.

`EmployeeRow`, `mapRow`, `create`, `findById`, `findByEmployeeNumber`, and `findByEmail` all select and map the new `password_hash` column so a persisted employee round-trips `passwordHash` correctly.
`IEmployeeService.getEmployeeByEmail(email)` returns the employee found via `repository.findByEmail`, and throws `NotFoundError('Employee not found')` when the lookup returns null.
`IEmployeeService.getEmployeesByManagerId(managerId)` returns `repository.findByManagerId(managerId)` unchanged (array, possibly empty, no error on empty).

constraints: The migration must use `t.text('password_hash')` (NOT `t.json`/`t.jsonb`), matching the existing `audit_logs.before_state`/`after_state` text-column convention in migrations/20260913000000_initial_schema.js.
`passwordHash` is a canonical model field but must never be serialized into any response body; this phase only adds the field and read paths — no route may expose it.
All database access stays behind the repository: `findByManagerId` is the only new SQL, and it must be a parameterized `SELECT ... WHERE manager_id = $1` mapped via the existing `mapRow`.

New repository/service methods accept an optional trailing `PoolClient` and fall back to the shared pool when omitted (per AGENTS.md transaction-boundary rule), even though this phase's operations are read-only and open no transaction.
outOfScope: No routes, controllers, or the `GET /employees/me` endpoint — that is Phase 7.
No auth/login logic, bcrypt hashing, or token minting — that is Phase 4; this phase only stores/reads the nullable hash.
No audit-log writes (GP-002) — this phase is read-only plus a schema change; no state-changing service operation is introduced.
No `manager_id` index creation or any other schema change beyond the nullable `password_hash` column.

ambiguities.description: Whether `create` should accept a `passwordHash` value from `CreateEmployeeInput` or always insert `null` for the new column (the phase says "update create to select and map password_hash" but does not say whether callers may set it).
options: create always inserts null for password_hash (callers cannot set it this phase)
create inserts input.passwordHash when present, else null

ambiguities.description: Whether the migration should also add the `manager_id` index noted in the reconciled schema (indexes: manager_id "currently unindexed and must be added") or leave it out of this phase.
options: Add the manager_id index in this migration
Leave the index out (out of scope; only the password_hash column)

entityInvariants.invariant: An Employee may carry a nullable credential (`passwordHash: string | null`); null means "no local password set". The field is canonical on the entity but is never serialized into any response body.
`managerId` is the single source of the direct-report relationship: `findByManagerId` returns exactly the employees whose `manager_id` equals the given id (one level, not transitive).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array (possibly empty); never throws on an empty result set.
Throws NotFoundError('Employee not found') when the repository returns null; otherwise returns the Employee.
Returns the repository result unchanged (array, possibly empty); never throws on empty.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The migration's `up`/`down` shape and column style must follow the existing initial-schema migration (alterTable add column in up, drop column in down; text column for a string payload).

`EmployeeRow`/`mapRow` must map `password_hash` → `passwordHash` exactly as the existing snake_case→camelCase mapping does for the other columns, and `create`/`findById`/`findByEmployeeNumber`/`findByEmail` must include `password_hash` in their SELECT/RETURNING lists.
`getEmployeeByEmail` must reuse the existing `NotFoundError` class and message convention already used by `getEmployeeById` ('Employee not found').
The `Employee` model's `passwordHash` field must match the reconciled entity shape (`passwordHash: string | null`) and the `CreateEmployeeInput = Omit<Employee, 'id'>` derivation must be preserved.

integrationPoints.why: The new repository/service methods must be reachable through the public entry point so Phase 4 (auth) and Phase 6 (leave list) can consume getEmployeeByEmail/getEmployeesByManagerId without importing internals.
findByManagerId and the updated read methods fall back to the shared pool when no client is supplied, matching the existing repository's `db(client)` pattern.
